/-- **The degree vanishes on classes pulled back from the base field**: `Spec K` is a
one-point space, so its Čech Picard group is trivial and every class of `picFromBase` is
trivial. -/
theorem classDeg_eq_zero_of_mem_picFromBase {K : Type u} [Field K] [Algebra k K]
    {L : (C ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic} (hL : L ∈ picFromBase C (overSpec k K)) :
    classDeg K L = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨N, rfl⟩ := (mem_picFromBase_iff C).mp hL
  haveI : Subsingleton (overSpec k K).left :=
    inferInstanceAs (Subsingleton (PrimeSpectrum K))
  rw [Scheme.CechPic.eq_one_of_subsingleton (overSpec k K).left N, map_one, classDeg_one]

/-! ## The relative degree -/

/-- **The degree on the relative Picard group over a field** (worksheet SB-5, first descent
gadget): `classDeg K` descends along `relPicMk` to the quotient
`relPic C (overSpec k K) = CechPic(C_K) ⧸ picFromBase`, because the Čech Picard group of the
one-point scheme `Spec K` is trivial.  The `degAt` brick (SB-6) reads the degree of a
field-representative of an étale-locally-trivial class through this homomorphism. -/

9	# The Galois splitting of the self-tensor `L ⊗[K] L ≃ Gal(L/K) → L`
10	
11	For a **finite Galois** extension `L/K` with group `G = Gal(L/K) = L ≃ₐ[K] L`, the
12	`L`-algebra map
13	
14	`a ⊗ b ↦ (γ ↦ a * γ b) : L ⊗[K] L → (G → L)`
15	
16	is an isomorphism (`galoisSelfTensorEquiv`).  Geometrically this is the statement
17	that `Spec L ×_{Spec K} Spec L` is `G` copies of `Spec L` — the fact that makes
18	the two pullback legs of a one-element Galois cover computable, and hence the
19	algebra input of the *invariance* half of Galois descent for the étale-sheafified
20	relative Picard functor.
21	
22	## Why this file exists
23	
24	`Picard/EtaleFieldCover.lean` builds the covering sieve generated by the single
25	morphism `Spec k' ⟶ Spec k`, and `Picard/PicEtDescentAssembly.lean` proves that a
26	*compatible family* on that cover has a unique amalgamation.  What stands between
27	a `Gal(k'/k)`-**invariant** `k'`-class and such a compatible family is agreement
28	on the two pullback legs of the sieve, and those legs live over
29	`Spec (k' ⊗[k] k')`.  Identifying that ring with `Gal(k'/k) → k'` is what turns
30	the group-theoretic hypothesis (invariance under each `γ`) into the sheaf-theoretic
31	one (agreement of two restrictions).
32	
33	Measured absent before being built (`ajc-p1`, run 0083 r6, and independently by
34	`ajc-p2` in inbox `I-1367`): `exact?` fails on `Function.Bijective` of exactly
35	this map, and no name-shaped search over Mathlib or either project returns it.
36	Mathlib's two nearest relatives are genuinely different statements:
37	
38	* `Algebra.Etale.iff_exists_algEquiv_prod` — an étale algebra is *some* finite
39	  product of finite separable extensions, with no identification of the index set
40	  with `Gal(L/K)` and no formula for the map;
41	* `Algebra.FormallyEtale.equivPiOfIsSepClosed` (`Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Field.lean`)
42	  — splits an étale algebra over a **separably closed** base, which is not the
43	  hypothesis here (if `K` were separably closed, `L = K`).
44	
45	## Main results
46	
47	* `galoisSelfTensorHom` — the `L`-algebra homomorphism `a ⊗ b ↦ (γ ↦ a * γ b)`.
48	* `galoisSelfTensorHom_bijective` — it is bijective.
49	* `galoisSelfTensorEquiv` — the resulting `L`-algebra equivalence, with
50	  `galoisSelfTensorEquiv_tmul` and `galoisSelfTensorEquiv_apply_tmul` for computing.
51	* `card_aut_eq_finrank_of_galoisSelfTensorHom_bijective` — the converse dimension
52	  count, and
53	* `galoisSelfTensorHom_bijective_iff_isGalois` — bijectivity **iff** Galois, for an
54	  arbitrary finite extension, which is what makes `[IsGalois K L]` the theorem's
55	  content rather than a hypothesis it merely uses.
56	
57	## Proof
58	
59	Surjectivity is Dedekind independence in the *column* form already in this
60	directory: `galoisCol_span` (`GaloisDescent/SemilinearModules.lean`) says the
61	vectors `(γ ↦ γ (b i))` span `G → L` over `L` for a `K`-basis `b` of `L`, and
62	those vectors are exactly the images `galoisSelfTensorHom (1 ⊗ₜ b i)`.  Injectivity
63	is then a dimension count: both sides have `L`-dimension `[L : K]`
64	(`Module.finrank_baseChange` on the left, `#G = [L:K]` on the right by
65	`IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank`), so a surjective `L`-linear map between them is
66	injective.
67	
68	No hypothesis beyond `[FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L]`, and in particular
69	nothing about `K` being perfect or separably closed.
70	
71	## What is measured, and what it does NOT buy
72	
73	Every declaration here is `sorry`-free and axiom-clean
74	`[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]`, against
75	`Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` as a control that correctly reports `sorryAx`

79	**Non-vacuity is measured at a nontrivial extension, not argued.** Three probes at

/-!
# `hcov` is a purely set-theoretic condition: joint surjectivity

`Picard/GaloisDescent/PicEtGaloisBridge.lean` §4 leaves one antecedent,
`hcov`, undischarged, and four landed `sorry`-free theorems carry it:
`projections_agree_of_invariant`, `exists_unique_descend_picEt_of_invariant`,
and the two assembly theorems of `Picard/PicEtDescentRepresentability.lean`.
`hcov` says the `Gal(k'/k)`-indexed family of sections
`coverSelfSection T γ = ⟨𝟙, twist γ⟩ : T_{k'} ⟶ T_{k'} ×_T T_{k'}`
generates a covering sieve of the étale topology on the slice over `Spec k`.

**This file reduces `hcov` to joint surjectivity of that family on points, with
nothing else owed** (`hcov_of_jointlySurjective`). The morphism-property half —
which the board and `PicEtGaloisBridge.lean`'s own `hcov_iff_scheme_level`
docstring both priced as *genuinely owed* — is **free**, and the reason is not
the one those sites were looking for.

## The repricing, and it is the finding

`I-1458` (and the corrected `hcov_iff_scheme_level` docstring after it) split
`hcov` into a *topology* half, declared free, and an *open-immersion* half,
declared owed: "the open-immersion half is genuinely owed — but a failed
`infer_instance` is not absence: `IsOpenImmersion (Sigma.ι …)` is a *theorem*
… where that theorem applies". The prescription was therefore to base-change
`selfTensorSpecCoproduct` along `T_{k'} ⟶ Spec k'` and match the coproduct's
`γ`-component to `coverSelfSection T γ`.

**None of that is needed.** The étale topology's covering criterion
(`Scheme.ofArrows_mem_precoverage_iff`) asks for `Etale` of each member, *not*
`IsOpenImmersion`; and `Etale` of a section is free by post-composition
cancellation, because `Etale` carries
`MorphismProperty.HasOfPostcompProperty @Etale`:

* `coverSelfSection T γ ≫ pullback.fst = 𝟙` (`coverSelfSection_fst`), so on
  underlying schemes the composite is `𝟙`, which is `Etale`;
* `(pullback.fst _ _).left` is `Etale`, being a base change of
  `(coverMap T).left = pullback.fst T.hom (specMapAlgebra k k')`
  (`etale_pullback_fst_specMap`) — and `Over.forget` sends the slice pullback
  to a scheme pullback, since pullback is a connected shape;
* cancelling the second factor gives `Etale (coverSelfSection T γ).left`.

So the coproduct splitting, `selfTensorSpecCoproduct`, `IsGalois` and
`sigmaSpec` are **all** absent from this file: nothing here needs the Galois
level, and `etale_coverSelfSection_left` holds for an arbitrary finite
separable `k'/k` and an arbitrary test `T`. Do not budget a coproduct
base-change argument for `hcov`.

**Why `IsOpenImmersion` was the wrong target — and the first version of this
paragraph got the reason wrong, which matters more than the conclusion**
(`I-1510`, `I-1513`; refuted by a fresh-context audit and reproduced here as
`isOpenImmersion_coverSelfSection_left`). That version said `IsOpenImmersion` is
"*strictly* stronger than the site asks for … and it is the one that fails
`infer_instance` while the cheap one does not". **Both halves are false.**

* `IsOpenImmersion` is **not** strictly stronger here: it is *equivalent*, and
  provable in three lines **from `etale_coverSelfSection_left` itself**. `Etale`
  gives `Flat` and `LocallyOfFinitePresentation` by synthesis, the section
  identity gives `Mono` by `mono_of_mono_fac`, and
  `IsOpenImmersion.of_flat_of_mono` closes it. So the withdrawn prescription was
  not *more expensive* — it was **less direct**, and it is a corollary of the
  cheap route rather than an alternative to it.
* `infer_instance` fails on the **`Etale`** goal too. There is no synthesis
  asymmetry, so the sentence that made the withdrawal read as *measured* was
  measuring nothing.

What survives, and it is the whole content: the étale site's criterion asks for
`Etale`, and `Etale` of a section is one cancellation, so **no coproduct
base-change is needed for the morphism-property half**. That is a
cheapest-route finding, not a strictness ordering. The general-`γ` route to
`IsOpenImmersion` is `of_flat_of_mono`; "the diagonal of an unramified morphism
is one" — the justification the first version offered — only applies at
`γ = 1`, where `coverSelfSection_one` puts the section at the diagonal.

`hcov_of_jointlySurjective`'s hypothesis: every point of
`(T_{k'} ×_T T_{k'}).left` is in the image of some `(coverSelfSection T γ).left`.
That is one statement about points, with no morphism property, no sieve, no
`picEt` and no slice in it. At a nontrivial Galois level it is the honest
content of `hcov` and it is **not** discharged here.

`I-1454` remains in force about the degenerate witness: at
`Mono (specMapAlgebra k k')` joint surjectivity holds for the trivial reason
that `coverSelfSection T 1` is an isomorphism, and there the *consequent* of §4
is free too. So this file does not exhibit a non-degenerate model; it removes
one of the two things a lane building one would have had to pay for.

## The route to joint surjectivity, measured link by link

Not built here, but every link probed to exist (`lake env lean` `EXIT=0`), so a
lane closing this owes no search:

1. `AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackSpecIso k k' k'` — Mathlib, and in *exactly* the

2. Composed with `selfTensorSpecCoproduct` (already in

   self-pullback **is** the `Gal`-indexed coproduct of copies of `Spec k'`, and
   the comparison is `IsIso` by synthesis.
3. `Scheme` is `FinitaryPreExtensive` **by synthesis**, and
   `CategoryTheory.FinitaryPreExtensive.isIso_sigmaDesc_fst` is the lemma that
   distributes a pullback over that coproduct. No new extensivity lemma is

   `AlgebraicGeometry.prod_coproduct_distrib` /`coprodFirst_distrib`

   inherit this step rather than removing it).

88	/-! ## §1. Transport along an equivariant isomorphism -/
89	
90	/-- **`IsGaloisQuotient` is invariant under an equivariant isomorphism of the acted scheme.**
91	
92	If `e : X ≅ X'` is a morphism over `Spec L` (`hef`) intertwining the two semilinear actions
93	(`he`), then `(Y, g)` is a Galois quotient of `(X', ρ')` iff it is one of `(X, ρ)`; this is the
94	direction that is used.
95	
96	Nothing here is about schemes over a field beyond the shape of `IsGaloisQuotient`: clause 1 is
97	a triangle, clause 2 the equivariance square (this is where `he` is spent), and clause 3 the
98	universal property, which transports by composing the test morphism with `e.hom` in one
99	direction and `e.inv` in the other. -/
100	theorem isGaloisQuotient_congr {X X' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
101	    {f' : X' ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)}
102	    (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f) (ρ' : SemilinearGalAction K L X' f')
103	    (e : X ≅ X') (hef : e.hom ≫ f' = f) (he : ρ.IsEquivariant ρ' e.hom)
104	    {Y : Scheme.{u}} {g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)}
105	    (h : IsGaloisQuotient ρ' g) : IsGaloisQuotient ρ g := by
106	  obtain ⟨d, hover, hequiv, huniv⟩ := h
107	  refine ⟨d ≪≫ e.symm, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
108	  · rw [Iso.trans_hom, Category.assoc, ← hef, Iso.symm_hom,
109	      Iso.inv_hom_id_assoc, hover]
110	  · intro γ
111	    have hinv : e.inv ≫ (ρ.act γ).hom = (ρ'.act γ).hom ≫ e.inv := by
112	      rw [Iso.inv_comp_eq, ← Category.assoc, ← he γ, Category.assoc,
113	        Iso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
114	    change _ ≫ d.hom ≫ e.inv = (d.hom ≫ e.inv) ≫ _
115	    rw [← Category.assoc, hequiv γ, Category.assoc, Category.assoc, hinv]
116	  · intro T t hh hover' hequiv'
117	    obtain ⟨u, hu, hu2⟩ := huniv T t (hh ≫ e.hom)
118	      (by rw [Category.assoc, hef, hover'])
119	      (by
120	        intro γ
121	        rw [← Category.assoc, hequiv' γ, Category.assoc, he γ, Category.assoc])
122	    refine ⟨u, ?_, fun v hv => hu2 v ?_⟩
123	    · change _ ≫ d.hom ≫ e.inv = hh
124	      rw [← Category.assoc, hu, Category.assoc, Iso.hom_inv_id, Category.comp_id]
125	    · change _ ≫ d.hom = hh ≫ e.hom
126	      have hv' : pullbackBaseChange K L g t v.1 v.2 ≫ d.hom ≫ e.inv = hh := hv
127	      rw [← Category.assoc] at hv'
128	      rw [← hv', Category.assoc, Iso.inv_hom_id, Category.comp_id]
129	
130	/-! ## §2. The affine case of the `G2` gate -/
131	
132	/-- **The Galois quotient exists for every semilinear action on an affine scheme**, with
133	`Spec (Γ(X, ⊤)^Γ) ⟶ Spec K` as the quotient.
134	
135	The route: `⊤` is `Γ`-stable, so the layer-1 substrate of
136	`Picard/GaloisQuotientGlue.lean` equips `Γ(X, ⊤)` with a semilinear `Γ`-action by ring
137	automorphisms over the `L`-algebra structure coming from `f` — the affine model's input format
138	— and `X.isoSpec` is then an equivariant isomorphism over `Spec L` from `ρ` to that model, so
139	`isGaloisQuotient_spec` transports by §1.
140	
141	Note the shape of the equivariance step: the section transport `ρ.actApp hU γ` of the action is
142	`(ρ.act γ).hom.appTop` composed with an identity restriction map, so mathlib's
143	`Scheme.isoSpec_hom_naturality` supplies the square directly. -/
144	theorem exists_isGaloisQuotient_of_isAffine {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsAffine X]
145	    {f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of L)} (ρ : SemilinearGalAction K L X f)
146	    [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsGalois K L] :
147	    ∃ (Y : Scheme.{u}) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)), IsGaloisQuotient ρ g := by
148	  have hU : ρ.IsStableOpen ⊤ := fun _ => rfl
149	  letI := ρ.sectionsMulSemiringAction hU
150	  letI := SemilinearGalAction.sectionsAlgebra f (⊤ : X.Opens)
151	  letI := SemilinearGalAction.sectionsAlgebraK (K := K) f (⊤ : X.Opens)
152	  haveI := SemilinearGalAction.sections_isScalarTower (K := K) f (⊤ : X.Opens)
153	  haveI := ρ.isSemilinear_sections hU
154	  refine ⟨Spec (CommRingCat.of
155	      (SemilinearAction.invariantsSubalgebra K L (Γ(X, ⊤) : Type u))),
156	    Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap K
157	      (SemilinearAction.invariantsSubalgebra K L (Γ(X, ⊤) : Type u)))), ?_⟩
158	  -- the affine model at `A = Γ(X, ⊤)` has a quotient (Speiser descent)
